chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Muhammad bin Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'And what thing is more delighting to my eyes than the dissimulation (Taqiyya)? Indeed, the dissimulation is a shield of the believer.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or prudence in concealing one's faith or beliefs to avoid harm

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyya as a shield for the believer according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), expressed great delight in the practice of Taqiyya, describing it as the shield that protects the believer. This narration underscores Taqiyya not merely as a defensive tactic during periods of persecution, but as a fundamental spiritual virtue and a means of preserving religious identity within the Shia tradition. It highlights the continuity of this principle from the Imams to the broader community as a safeguard against external threats to faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Myasws fatherasws was saying: ‘And which thing is more delighting to myasws eyes than the dissimulation (Taqiyya). The dissimulation (Taqiyya) is a shield of the Momin’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Marwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
My father (a.s.) has said, ‘What could be more delightful to me than al-Taqiyyah’, it is a shield for believing people.’”
